The main takeaway from our work is that

the brain can estimate the speed of a complex naturalistic scene by normalizing the activity in a set of channels, and that this normalization mechanism is implemented by a combination of two factors: a slow speed prior and a lateral inhibition mechanism.

the brain may not only use a set of channels to estimate speed, but also normalize the output of these channels in order to obtain an estimate that is robust to changes in the spatial frequency content of the input.
the visual system can estimate speed across scales and speeds by normalizing the response in each spatiotemporeal channel with respect to the response in other channels.
